statement: For every pair of integers m,n>=4, assign independent rate-one exponential costs to the edges of K_{m,n}, and let C_{4,m,n} be the minimum total cost of a matching of four edges. Then F_{4,m,n}(t)=E exp(t C_{4,m,n}) is nonzero for every complex t with |t|<mn/4. Moreover, every zero of the reduced numerator of its rational continuation has modulus strictly greater than mn/4. The proof establishes the stronger algebraic statement that the explicit sextic P_{m,n} in evidence/k4-proof.md has no root in |t|<=mn/4 for all real m,n>=4, using F_{4,m,n}=A P_{m,n}/Q for integer parameters. Boundary poles are not claimed to be finite nonzero values. The frozen conjecture for unrestricted k remains unresolved.
contribution: Uniform zero exclusion for the full k=4 parameter range, extending the k<=3 zero-free theorem in the inspected Wastlund arXiv:2602.07563v1. The proof gives an exact coefficient-positivity certificate for all six Hurwitz minors of a transformed sextic, reconstructed and checked with two separate arithmetic implementations. Explicit computability of the k=4 distribution and the classical Hurwitz criterion are prior work. No equivalent zero-exclusion theorem was identified in the bounded primary-source screen; global priority and fresh mathematical acceptance are not claimed.
